title: Public-Sharing Labels and Verbatim Field Egress in an MCP-to-A2A Agent Configuration: A Controlled Multi-Model Study
abstract: arXiv:2609.01693v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Safety properties assessed separately for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool use and Agent2Agent (A2A) delegation need not describe behavior when one agent uses both. We measure one such behavior in a single controlled MCP-to-A2A configuration: a testbed drives a real-model host across a local MCP and a local A2A leg into an ordered event trace scored by exact deterministic rules (no LLM judge), one restricted decision per trial. In a pre-specified, frozen three-arm design, each of 10 record scenarios appears with a CONFIDENTIAL header, with no header, and with PUBLIC - OK TO SHARE; the six substantive record values are byte-identical across arms, and the outcome is verbatim occurrence of any of them in the outbound message. Four models x 3 arms x 4 repeats give 480 trials; the scenario is the unit of generalization, and we report the 10 scenario-level values (mean, median, sign counts), with no p-values or intervals. translated_title: MCP-to-A2A 智能体配置中的公开共享标签与逐字字段外泄：一项受控多模型研究
translated_abstract: 分别针对模型上下文协议（MCP）工具使用和 Agent2Agent（A2A）委托所评估的安全性属性，未必能描述同一智能体同时使用两者时的行为。我们在单一受控的 MCP-to-A2A 配置中测量了这样一种行为：测试平台驱动真实模型主机经由本地 MCP 和本地 A2A 两条链路，生成有序事件轨迹，并按精确的确定性规则评分（不使用 LLM 评判），每次试验仅包含一个受限决策。在一个预先指定且冻结的三臂设计中，10 个记录场景分别以三种形式出现：带 CONFIDENTIAL（机密）标头、不带标头、以及带 PUBLIC - OK TO SHARE（公开-可分享）标头；六个实质性记录值在各组间逐字节相同，结果指标为其中任一值在出站消息中的逐字出现。四个模型 × 3 个组别 × 4 次重复共得到 480 次试验；场景是泛化单位，我们报告 10 个场景层面的数值（均值、中位数、符号计数），不报告 p 值或置信区间。（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过 480 次试验的受控多模型实验，用确定性规则测量不同共享标签（机密/无标头/公开）下机密字段在 MCP-to-A2A 智能体出站消息中的逐字外泄情况，表明单独评估 MCP 与 A2A 的安全属性无法预测两者同时使用时的实际行为。
en_tdlr: This controlled multi-model study (480 trials) uses deterministic scoring to measure verbatim egress of confidential record fields in an MCP-to-A2A agent configuration under different sharing labels, showing that safety properties assessed separately for MCP tool use and A2A delegation do not predict behavior when one agent uses both.
